english: The guests are coming. Prepare the enclosure, and I will slaughter the lamb. Let the cook cook it. It is getting dark; let the fire burn. Who is coming? The king is coming, and the queen is with him. Now let us go, give wine and beer, and let there be good songs. Sit. The work has succeeded. I have toiled and I rejoice. Those (two?) are sated. Daughter-in-law, bring, bring wine; son-in-law, beer. Who is this woman? This is my daughter-in-law, and that is my son-in-law.
uncertain: tóy séh2etes: masc. pl. pronoun with a 2/3du verb, number unclear

english: Daughter-in-law, come. I am your husband's mother. I was afraid. Daughter-in-law, do not fear. This house of yours is dear, and I protect you. Your husband is dear to us, and he loves you. I toiled(?). I clothe you with wool. Take the ornament and wear it. Your words are fresh and sweet. I welcome/desire you. See that field and that hill. Your husband ploughs. I work. Who is that man? That is your brother-in-law.
uncertain: bhebhóyh2h2e: 1sg perfect 'I have feared' - who fears is unclear

english: Whom do you desire, swift one? I desire her who lives by the river. Her father is a herdsman. Does she desire you? I do not know. Now seek her and speak. She will listen. I go to the river and speak to her father. Take a good lamb and silver. Say your name and he will see it. Your name is famous. I am afraid. Do not tremble. I will make an ornament for her.
uncertain: tód-kʷe h2wéyseti 'and he will see it' vs 'it will be seen'

english: Brother, wake up, dawn has shone. I wake and tremble. I saw a snake in a dream. It crawled toward our house. Brother, do not fear; a dream does not kill. I have feared (?) your heart, and my (heart) trembles. Stand and put on your wool. We two go to the stream and drink. If the snake comes, I will kill it. Brother, you grew up and did not fear. The snake is seeking(?). We two go to the hill and look.
uncertain: bhebhóydhh2e toy ḱḗr: 1sg perfect with 'your heart' as apparent subject - looks like a person error (3sg bhebhóydhe expected)

english: Who is Mother Earth? Earth is the mother of mortals. She protects them, and Sky is their father. Where is Sky? Sky is above, and Earth is below. Does Sky hear us? He hears and has seen. I speak. Speak, and he will see. Who is Perkunos? Perkunos is a god. When Perkunos comes, he rains, and the earth (is) in rain(?). Is the sun a god? The sun brings light and warms the earth.
uncertain: dyḗws kúdhe h1stés: 2/3du verb with singular Sky
dhéǵhōm (nom.) as object of gʷhr̥néwti and h2wérseti

english: Night is coming and I tremble. Do not fear. The dog guards the enclosure. Lie down and hear my song. What stands? The tree stands. What ran? The stream ran. What burns? The fire burns. What grew? The grain grew. Who died? The mortal died. The god did not die. I hear. Is the snake near? The snake does not crawl. May a good dream come to you. Dawn will shine and you will see the sun. The duck lies on the water, the snake lies, and the wild beast is away.
uncertain: kʷéḱesi read as 2sg future 'you will see'
